description: Zeck free-tier-first provider topology ledger (DEP-001). Records, for every provider in providers.json, the tier the public deployment bootstrap selects under the roadmap doctrine order (provider free tier -> usage-based/no-minimum -> low fixed-cost managed -> paid only where required), the CURRENT limits/terms as operational constraints, the degradation path on exhaustion/outage, and the explicit upgrade/exit note. Limits are external facts recorded with an asOf date and a verification status; they are NEVER architecture. Live verification of provider consoles was NOT RUN in the DEP-001 worker pod (no credentials) — every entry carries verification 'recorded-not-live-verified' and must be re-verified by the credentialed operator at dispatch time (DEP-001 AC7 / roadmap free-tier doctrine).

verification.detail: Limits below were recorded from the providers' public documentation knowledge at authoring time (asOf). NOT RUN: no provider console, quota API or live deployment was queried from the DEP-001 worker pod — no cloud credentials exist there (DEP-001 AC7). The credentialed operator (Lead re-run) must re-verify each limit against the provider's current pricing/limits page before applying the deployment; drift is an operational update to this ledger, never a silent assumption.

selectedTier.selectionRationale: Doctrine position 1 (provider free tier): the authoritative relational concern runs on Neon Free for preview/sandbox exploration; PostgreSQL remains the only durable authority.

limits.value: bounded free compute hours per month (plan-defined)

tiers.limitsSource: Neon public pricing documentation (recorded at asOf; not live-verified in this pod)
tiers.terms: Free tier is for development/evaluation use; production commercial use should move to a paid plan (e.g. Neon Launch) per provider terms.
tiers.upgradeExit: The authoritative concern MUST NOT remain on the free tier for commercial production: promote to Neon Launch (or any managed PostgreSQL provider — the adapter is provider-neutral over the PostgreSQL wire protocol; connection URLs only). Exit path: pg_dump/logical backup through deploy:backup, restore into the replacement through deploy:restore — both are repository-resident drills. The database-port contract (src/platform/db/port.ts) is unchanged by the move.

exhaustionBehavior.effect: Storage/compute exhaustion on the authoritative store fails closed: control-plane admission and every authority-bearing operation refuse. No datastore is silently promoted; no silent paid overage is enabled by default (Neon Free overage is disabled by design; the quota fence denies at the declared limit).

selectedTier.selectionRationale: Doctrine position 1 (provider free tier): artifact bytes (non-authoritative; metadata stays in PostgreSQL) fit the R2 free allowances for preview/sandbox volumes.

tiers.limitsSource: Cloudflare R2 public pricing documentation (recorded at asOf; not live-verified in this pod)
tiers.terms: R2 free allowances apply on any plan; usage beyond allowances bills usage-based (no fixed minimum).
tiers.upgradeExit: Non-authoritative bytes: exit to any S3-compatible object store through the D-07 artifact-exit drill (deploy:drill artifact-exit — digest-verified byte migration over two ObjectStorePort endpoints; endpoint+credentials only). The free allowance is disposable headroom, never an operational dependency: artifact metadata/provenance stay authoritative in PostgreSQL.

exhaustionBehavior.effect: Operations requiring artifact bytes fail explicitly; metadata and provenance remain authoritative in PostgreSQL. No artifact bytes fall back through PostgreSQL. Paid overage beyond the free allowance requires the explicit recorded opt-in (quota fence); the default is deny-at-limit.

selectedTier.selectionRationale: Doctrine position 2 (usage-based/no-minimum): Queues bills per operation with no fixed minimum; the dispatch transport is non-authoritative and backlogs safely in PostgreSQL.

limits.value: usage-based per million operations (no fixed minimum)
provider-defined per-message bound (envelopes carry reference-only correlation pointers)

tiers.limitsSource: Cloudflare Queues public pricing documentation (recorded at asOf; not live-verified in this pod)
tiers.terms: Usage-based billing on the owning Cloudflare account; throughput/concurrency subject to plan limits.
tiers.upgradeExit: Non-authoritative transport: exit to any managed queue/broker implementing the QueueTransportPort contract through the queue-recovery drill (transport substitution + replay convergence through existing dispatch/execution idempotency). Backlogged dispatch is recoverable by design (deploy:queue republish/replay).

exhaustionBehavior.effect: Execution admission continues through PostgreSQL authority; dispatch defers and backlogs. A queued message is never mistaken for execution success. Spend guardrail: publish attempts are bounded (ZECK_QUEUE_MAX_PUBLISH_ATTEMPTS); the quota fence denies further publishes at the declared spend limit rather than silently continuing paid operations.

selectedTier.selectionRationale: Doctrine position 2 (usage-based/no-minimum): orchestration is non-authoritative and pauses safely; Workflows bills per invocation/duration with no fixed minimum.

limits.value: usage-based per million invocations (no fixed minimum)
30 days (documented provider retention; orphaned instances are bounded waste)

tiers.limitsSource: Cloudflare Workflows public pricing documentation (recorded at asOf; not live-verified in this pod)
tiers.terms: Usage-based billing on the owning Cloudflare account; requires a deployed Worker script (Workers Scripts Write token).
tiers.upgradeExit: Non-authoritative orchestration: exit to any durable workflow engine implementing the workflow port contract. Waiting executions live in PostgreSQL (workflow_orchestration.waits is the authority); instances are terminated by compaction and the replacement engine is re-armed by the recovery scan.

exhaustionBehavior.effect: Waiting orchestrations pause; execution status, budget, policy and ledger state remain authoritative in PostgreSQL and resume on recovery. Instance starts are bounded (ZECK_WORKFLOW_MAX_START_ATTEMPTS); the quota fence denies at the declared spend limit.

selectedTier.selectionRationale: Doctrine position 1 (provider free tier): coordination data is recomputable/bounded/expiring — the textbook free-tier-safe workload.

tiers.limitsSource: Upstash public pricing documentation (recorded at asOf; not live-verified in this pod)
tiers.terms: Free tier for evaluation/development; pay-as-you-go beyond.
tiers.upgradeExit: Disposable by doctrine: Redis holds NO authority data (locks, rate limits, dedup hints, cache only). Exit is dropping it — the coordination-degraded mode is a first-class operating state (local runs without Redis by default). Replacement: any managed Redis-compatible service (or local Redis) behind src/platform/redis/port.ts.

exhaustionBehavior.effect: Command-quota exhaustion or outage degrades to conservative local behavior; durable authority is untouched. The daily command quota makes exhaustion a routine expected state, not an incident.

selectedTier.selectionRationale: Doctrine position 1 (provider free tier) FOR PREVIEW/PERSONAL-NON-COMMERCIAL ONLY: the terms restriction is the binding constraint (ACR-002: Hobby is a development/non-commercial facility; free-tier claims are never commercial entitlements).

limits.value: PROHIBITED — personal/non-commercial development and preview only

tiers.limitsSource: Vercel public pricing documentation (recorded at asOf; not live-verified in this pod)
tiers.terms: Vercel Hobby is restricted to permitted personal/non-commercial use (repository contract, ACR-002, providers.json commercialUse). Commercial production MUST use a commercially permitted plan (Vercel Pro) or an alternate host.
tiers.upgradeExit: Delivery-only concern: the API is independently runnable (deploy/api.ts; D1.0 section 12) — repoint delivery at any host running the same repository entry with configuration only. Upgrade: Vercel Pro for commercial production; exit: any alternate web/API host (the redundancy alternate in providers.json). Domain authority is unchanged by the repoint (the domain is operator-owned config, never the provider's).

exhaustionBehavior.effect: Hobby bandwidth/function limits make the experience layer unreachable; control-plane and execution-plane authority are unaffected. The degradation is honest at /health (delivery-degraded) and the operator repoints or upgrades — no silent paid overage (Hobby does not overage bandwidth by default).

selectedTier.selectionRationale: Doctrine position 4 (paid only where required): execution compute is a capability/isolation requirement — container isolation cannot be safely satisfied by a shared free-tier HTTP host. The reference deployment self-hosts the runner (zero marginal provider cost) or binds governed customer runners.

limits.value: self-hosted runner cost only; no per-run provider fee

tiers.limitsSource: Repository-defined protocol (deploy/README.md container-runner REST contract); no external provider quota.
tiers.terms: First-party fleet runner or a governed customer runner implementing the documented protocol; Zeck validates configurations before the wire.
tiers.upgradeExit: Non-authoritative executor: any runner daemon implementing the documented REST protocol (provider-neutral, no vendor SDK). Absent runner = container substrate reports unavailable and dispatch fails closed; the process substrate still executes.

exhaustionBehavior.effect: Container sandbox dispatch fails closed (runtime-unavailable); executions stay durably recoverable in PostgreSQL and re-dispatch on recovery. No unisolated or ambient-host execution is ever a fallback.

selectedTier.selectionRationale: Doctrine position 2 (usage-based/no-minimum): OTLP/HTTP-JSON is a transport standard; a self-hosted collector (zero cost) or a usage-based managed sink both satisfy the port.

limits.value: bounded by repository constants (buffer maxima, batch sizes, retry attempts are hard-bounded)
self-hosted collector: zero provider cost; managed sink: usage-based

tiers.limitsSource: Repository-defined observability port (src/platform/observability/port.ts); no external provider quota.
tiers.terms: Any OpenTelemetry-compatible collector (self-hosted or managed); the protocol is a standard, not a vendor control plane.
tiers.upgradeExit: Unconfigured endpoint is the declared logs-only degraded mode — observability never blocks the control or execution planes. Substitution is endpoint configuration only.

exhaustionBehavior.effect: Endpoint unreachable or unconfigured: the sink degrades to bounded structured local logs with drop counters; overflow is dropped and counted, never buffered unbounded.
